title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten campus spaces with specific, documented uses for studying, relaxing, recreation, events, and commuter or first-generation student support.

cards.title: Settle In for a Game-Room Break
cards.subtitle: Lower level of the Sondra and David S. Mack Student Center
cards.notes: Bring your HofstraCard, then choose from console stations, pool, ping-pong, foosball, or board games between classes.
cards.short_summary: An ID-controlled student space that combines casual games, seating, lunch breaks, and homework.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra says the Game Room has consoles, pool tables, ping-pong, foosball, board games, and furniture for relaxing, eating lunch, or doing homework.
cards.source_title: Game Room | Student Leadership & Engagement | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Room 029, lower level of the Mack Student Center. Entry is limited to students and staff carrying a valid Hofstra ID; guests are not permitted.

cards.title: Use the Pride Den as a Flexible Hangout
cards.subtitle: Lower level of the Sondra and David S. Mack Student Center
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar before visiting; the den doubles as a lounge and a venue for student performances and programs.
cards.short_summary: A renovated student lounge that shifts between informal gathering space and scheduled campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra identifies the Pride Den as a key student lounge and says its renovation added furnishings, internet connections, and audiovisual components for study, collaboration, and entertainment.
cards.source_title: Construction and Projects Archives | Facilities & Operations | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of the Mack Student Center. Scheduled events may affect ordinary lounge use; consult Hofstra's event calendar.

cards.title: Keep a Late Study Session Grounded
cards.subtitle: First floor of the Sondra and David S. Mack Student Center
cards.notes: Use the lounge for reading, charging devices, watching television, or meeting someone when most daytime offices have closed.
cards.short_summary: A specifically designated round-the-clock lounge for breaks and low-key work in the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra's Commuting Student Services page lists the Mack Student Center 24-hour lounge, with television, among campus places for relaxing, reading, meeting friends, and charging devices.
cards.source_title: Services | Commuting Student Services | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: First floor beside the Student Center Theatre. Hofstra currently identifies it as a 24-hour lounge; building access rules still apply.

cards.title: Heat Lunch and Reset Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Room 221 in the Sondra and David S. Mack Student Center
cards.notes: Bring lunch to use the microwave, recharge during a long gap, or ask the commuter-services staff about lockers and campus resources.
cards.short_summary: A staffed commuter-focused lounge with practical amenities for students spending a full day on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra says the Room 221 lounge is open to students during posted hours and offers coffee or tea plus a microwave for heating lunch.
cards.source_title: Services | Commuting Student Services | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Room 221, Mack Student Center. Hofstra lists lounge access from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. when classes are in session; the office operates weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Switch to a Dedicated Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Across from the Axinn Library entrance on South Campus
cards.notes: Head here when your work needs a desktop, campus technology, or a setting separate from the library's reading areas.
cards.short_summary: A named computer lab positioned directly across from the main library entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra identifies Hammer Lab, across from the Axinn Library entrance on South Campus, as one of the campus lounge and work areas commuter students should know.
cards.source_title: Services | Commuting Student Services | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Located across from the Axinn Library entrance on South Campus. Verify current lab hours and HofstraCard access before planning an overnight session.

cards.title: Move Group Work to the Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the Joan and Donald E. Axinn Library
cards.notes: Meet here when a project benefits from conversation and shared work; choose another library area when you need individual quiet.
cards.short_summary: A library lounge specifically developed for collaborative learning rather than silent solo study.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra lists the Collaborative Learning Center on Axinn Library's second floor as a campus lounge, and its facilities archive says the space was created as a learning center and lounge.
cards.source_title: Construction and Projects Archives | Facilities & Operations | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Second floor of Axinn Library. Access follows current library building hours and University entry policies.

cards.title: Match Your Seat to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Tenth floor of the Joan and Donald E. Axinn Library
cards.notes: Choose an individual desk for focused work or use group desks and sofa-style seating when classmates need to collaborate.
cards.short_summary: A renovated upper-floor study area offering distinct seating modes for solo and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra reports that Axinn Library's renovated 10th floor is a dedicated collaborative and study space with individual and group desks, sofas, and egg chairs.
cards.source_title: Celebrating the Library's 10th Floor Renovation | Hofstra University News
cards.access_notes: Located on Axinn Library's 10th floor. Use is subject to current library hours, building policies, and any event reservations.

cards.title: Connect With First-Generation Support
cards.subtitle: Room 219 in the Sondra and David S. Mack Student Center
cards.notes: Stop in for first-generation programming and mentorship, and follow the office's official updates before attending a scheduled activity.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge where first-generation students can connect with support programs and mentors.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra identifies the First-Gen Lounge in Student Center Room 219 and says First-Generation Support and Engagement provides programming and mentorship.
cards.access_notes: Room 219, Mack Student Center. The official page does not publish regular drop-in hours; confirm access or program timing with First-Generation Support and Engagement.

cards.title: Take a Break on the Outdoor Courts
cards.subtitle: Beside the Wellness and Campus Living Center on North Campus
cards.notes: Check whether intramurals are scheduled, then bring classmates for basketball or use available RecRe Box equipment as directed.
cards.short_summary: Open student recreation courts with basketball facilities and app-accessible shared equipment nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Hofstra says the outdoor Multisport Courts are next to the Wellness Center, equipped for basketball, open for student use and intramurals, and served by a RecRe Box with borrowable gear.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor courts next to the Wellness and Campus Living Center on North Campus. Availability may change for intramurals, programs, or weather.

cards.title: Use the Gallery as a Class Extension
cards.subtitle: Hofstra University Museum of Art in Emily Lowe Hall
cards.notes: Visit during current gallery access periods, look closely at the changing exhibition, and use one object to prompt discussion or writing.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum gallery used for exhibitions, object study, class meetings, and interdisciplinary assignments.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hofstra University Museum of Art documents class meetings in the Emily Lowe Gallery and says its exhibitions support gallery teaching, tours, and permanent-collection object study.
cards.source_title: Museum Education – Hofstra Faculty | Hofstra University
cards.access_notes: Located in Emily Lowe Hall. Check the Museum's current exhibition schedule and access information; faculty-led class visits should be scheduled with Museum Education.
